content: Yellow Jessamine, scientifically known as Gelsemium sempervirens, is a twining vine that belongs to the family Gelsemiaceae. It is also commonly referred to as Evening Trumpetflower or Carolina Jessamine. This plant is native to warm temperate and tropical regions of the Americas, ranging from Guatemala to the southeastern United States. When provided with appropriate climbing support, such as trees, this vine can grow to a height of 3 to 6 meters. It has thin stems and dark green, lustrous leaves that are approximately 5 cm long and 3 cm wide. All parts of the Yellow Jessamine plant contain toxic alkaloids, specifically gelsemine and gelseminine, which are chemically related to strychnine. These compounds render the plant highly poisonous and unsuitable for consumption. Additionally, the sap of the plant can cause skin irritation in individuals with heightened sensitivity. Children have been poisoned by mistaking the flowers of Yellow Jessamine for honeysuckle and consuming the nectar. The nectar itself is toxic, not only to humans but also to honeybees. When honeybees collect this nectar, it can lead to brood death within the hive. Despite its toxic properties, Yellow Jessamine remains a popular ornamental plant in warmer climates. It is often cultivated to grow over arbors or to cover walls, adding aesthetic value to gardens. However, caution is advised due to its hazardous nature. Yellow Jessamine is the state flower of South Carolina. The flowers of this plant are not scented, and the nectar is located at the base of the flower.
